newsitem.title: NICARAGUA: Nicaraguan police tied to car-theft ring.
newsitem.headline: Nicaraguan police tied to car-theft ring.

text.p: Nicaragua's National Police on Thursday fired a top officer for involvement in an international ring that smuggled stolen cars from Honduras to Nicaragua.

Police Chief Franco Montealegre told a news conference that an internal police investigation found that Capt. Adan Cuadra, the force's top legal advisor, served as the Nicaraguan point man for a Honduran car-theft ring.
Cuadra was the first Nicaraguan police officer dishonourably discharged for involvement in the car-theft rings that plague Central America, Montealegre said.
Police corruption was "minimal" in Nicaragua, he added. "The police force is not corrupt and this case shows we are not going to accept corruption," he said.
As part of an anti-corruption campaign, Nicaraguan police have fired 22 officers in recent weeks on charges ranging from "administrative negligence" to accepting bribes.
Montealegre said police had connected Cuadra to the sale of four stolen cars smuggled into Nicaragua but would not say how many cars the ring had smuggled.

He said the cars were stolen in Honduras and arrived at the Nicaraguan border with Honduran registration papers. Cuadra acted as the gang's middleman, finding Nicaraguan buyers. Since the thefts and false registrations all occurred in Honduras, Cuadra cannot be prosecuted in Nicaragua, he said.
